title: Thinking levels on the frozen code
subtitle: How often FARM's generation gets the Reward Machine right at each thinking level, on the frozen code, with the production pair (generator deepseek-v4.1-flash, critic glm-5.3-flash): 46 task cases, 3 runs each. Right: 76% at none, 97% at low, 99% at medium, 100% at high and at max. Max takes about four times as long as high for the same score.

sections.title: Right machines per thinking level
sections.intro: 46 task cases, 3 runs each, at every thinking level of both models: 138 runs a level, 690 in all. A run is right when its final clause set is the card's answer or one of the answers the card also accepts (the next section says exactly how).

items: **Form A**: the scorer accepts the set but does not count it right (a "must happen" rule on an earlier step of an ordered task).
**First answer right**: the generator's first answer, before any critic feedback, scored the same way.

**Time**: from the start of generation to the accepted machine, per run; 8 runs went at once, beside 12 to 23 RL trainings, so it is not a clean speed measure. **Model calls**: generator plus critic requests, counted in the run records; they equal the call logs' counts in `stats.md`.

blocks.title: In plain words
blocks.text:
FARM turns a task written in English into Declare clauses (the generator), has a second model check them (the critic), and compiles the accepted clauses into a Reward Machine. This benchmark asks how often that machine is the right one when both models think less or more. Each of the 46 cases is one task card; every level ran every case 3 times on the code freeze `809dfe3` (minimization on by default), 690 runs in all, on 2026-11-22 between 08:49 and 10:06.

Without thinking (`none`) 33 of 138 runs end with a machine that is not right. With any thinking the generator's first answer was right in all 552 runs. The 6 wrong machines at low and medium came from the critic turning a right answer down. At high and max nothing went wrong.

items: **No thinking is not enough.** At `none` 31 runs are wrong and 2 are form A. The critic caught 19 of the 43 first answers that were not right; most of what it let through is about order: a soft ban read as an order (10 runs), a stated order dropped (12), an order the task does not state (5).

**Low and medium: the critic is the weak link.** Every first answer was right. In 6 runs (4 at low, 2 at medium) the critic rejected it and accepted a wrong second answer. Four of the six are G9, where the card and the critic read "Then" differently.

**High and max: 138 of 138 each.** Every first answer was accepted on the first critic call, 276 calls per level. Max took a median 88 s per run against 20 s at high, and 13,946 s in all against 3,573 s.

**Model side, not pipeline side.** Every machine that is not right comes from an accepted clause set the card rejects. Each machine on this page was compiled again from its run's clauses and gives the record's machine text. The two incidents of the run (the provider's rate limit, our budget guard) changed no answer.

blocks.text: The scorer is the loop's `chain_score.classify` (`check/chain_score.py`), the one that wrote `stats.md`. It compares a run's final clause set with the case's card. `check/cases.py` maps each case to a card; the cards are copied in `evidence/cards/`: those of main `e6c3acb`, plus the loop's local soft cards for S1 to S4.

items: **Right**: the set is the card's `expect` set or one of its `also_ok` sets (the repository's `clause_status`), or the `expect` set plus orders it implies. An implied order is a `Precedence` the card's hard orders give by chaining (key before goal when key before door before goal) and, on three cards the loop may not edit, an order the level forces. A set with an extra hard `Existence` that its orders already force is right once that clause is dropped, except on ordered cases.
**Form A**: on an ordered case, the set passes only with a hard `Existence` on an earlier step, one "must happen" rule per step instead of the chain. Counted apart, not right.
**Wrong**: anything else, or a run that ended with no accepted set.
**Clause lists, not tasks.** A wrong set can still describe a task close to the card's; the page says so where it applies (G4, G9).

blocks.title: G9: a card reading the critic does not share
blocks.text: G9 says "Whenever you are holding the key, the door must be open at that moment or opened afterwards. Then reach the goal." The card reads "Then" as an order from holding the key to the goal, `Response(has_key, at_goal)`; the critic reads it as after the door only. It is close to the open question in `stated-order-rule/`, whether "Then" after an if-rule orders the rule's steps.

blocks.heading: The critic's full reply on the right first answer

items.title: low G11-r2
items.text: CHANGES REQUIRED: the task is 'Never both drop the key while the door is still closed and open the door'. The ban's event key_lost is defined as 'previously acquired the key but is no longer carrying it before opening the door' — it already contains the 'while the door is still closed' condition, so the ban is a plain hard Absence(key_lost), not NotCoExistence(key_lost, door_open). The NotCoExistence clause wrongly forbids door_open ever, contradicting the command. Also, 'open the door' is an unconditional hard command, so a hard Existence(door_open) is needed and is missing (FINAL_STATES is empty). Replace the clause with hard Absence(key_lost) and hard Existence(door_open).

items.title: low G4-r3
items.text: CHANGES REQUIRED: the task states a three-step order — hold the key (twice), open the door, reach the goal — as steps in one sentence. The candidate captures the last link with hard Precedence(door_open, at_goal) and hard Existence(at_goal), and the first step with hard ExistenceTwo(has_key), but the link between has_key and door_open is missing: there is no Precedence(has_key, door_open). Although the environment constraint ('door_open cannot become true before has_key') makes the order hold in practice, an order the task states needs its Precedence clause even when the environment already guarantees it. Add a hard Precedence(has_key, door_open). Note also that the hard Existence(at_goal) is required here, since the first step is an ExistenceTwo(count) and the chain from has_key to at_goal is not a plain Precedence chain that forces at_goal without it — keeping it is correct.

items.title: low G9-r1
items.text: CHANGES REQUIRED: the hard Response(has_key, at_goal) (R4) is an added requirement. The task's 'whenever you are holding the key' clause concerns only the door being open at that moment or afterwards, which Response(has_key, door_open) already captures. 'Then reach the goal' is a separate command to reach the goal after opening the door, already covered by Existence(at_goal) and Precedence(door_open, at_goal). No sentence says that whenever the key is held, the goal must be reached afterwards. Remove Response(has_key, at_goal); keep the other three clauses.

items.title: low G9-r2
items.text: CHANGES REQUIRED: the hard Response(has_key, at_goal) ('Whenever the agent is holding the key, the goal must be reached at that moment or afterwards') is an added requirement: the task says only 'Whenever you are holding the key, the door must be open at that moment or opened afterwards. Then reach the goal.' It conditions the door on holding the key, not the goal. This clause also creates odd obligations (e.g., ending the episode while still holding the key with the goal just reached is fine, but the machine penalizes states the task does not constrain). Remove Response(has_key, at_goal); keep the hard Response(has_key, door_open), hard Existence(at_goal), and hard Precedence(door_open, at_goal).

items.title: medium G9-r1
items.text: CHANGES REQUIRED: the hard Response(has_key, at_goal) is an added requirement. The task says only 'Whenever you are holding the key, the door must be open at that moment or opened afterwards' (Response(has_key, door_open), correct, including as a lasting condition) and 'Then reach the goal' (hard Existence(at_goal), with Precedence(door_open, at_goal) recording the stated order). No sentence demands that the goal be reached at that moment or after every has_key; at_goal is not a consequent of the holding-key condition. Remove Response(has_key, at_goal); keep the other three clauses.

items.title: medium G9-r2

No sentence says the goal must be reached after holding the key. Remove Response(has_key, at_goal); keep Response(has_key, door_open), Existence(at_goal), and Precedence(door_open, at_goal).

items: **Rate limit at none.** 5 runs (G6-r3, G7-r1, G7-r2, G7-r3, G8-r1) stopped on the provider's HTTP 429 rate limit after 10 reruns, with no answer. Their records were renamed `*.json.429` and are kept in `records/none/`; the 5 runs were run again at 09:01 and all 5 were accepted. Their 55 refused requests are not in the 1,473 calls.

**Budget guard outlived its round.** The guard started for the low round kept watching after that round ended and wrote a STOP file at 09:00:20 (`evidence/STOP.guard-bug-0900`), which stopped the medium round after 14 runs (`evidence/round-logs/medium.log`). The driver now stops each level's guard when the level ends (`check/level-bench.sh`), and medium resumed at 09:02:26, skipping the runs already done.
One model pair through one provider (OpenCode), 3 runs per case and level: a case's 2 of 3 is a small sample.
The 46 cases are the generator loop's working set, picked around past mistakes (W, U), ordered tasks (O), guard cards (G) and soft last steps (S), not a random sample of tasks.
Times come from a shared machine: 8 runs at once beside 12 to 23 RL trainings.
The mistake groups at none are this entry's reading of the clause sets.
No call logs are copied, so output tokens and seconds per call are only in `stats.md`, which read them from the plan folder.

From the plan folder `farm-final-20261119/`: `bash freeze-prep/tools/level-bench.sh 8` ran the five levels in order, each as `bash until-fix/tools/run_arms.sh freeze-<level> <the 46 cases> A 3 8 <level>` (arm A, 3 runs per case, 8 at once).
